native_result.query: What is the proportion of junior professors in replicated studies in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, replicated studies have a much higher proportion of junior professor (64.7%) and in the original studies the senior professors are more represented (82.4%)
native_result.HypoB: Among the 90 non-dropped replication studies in the Psychology (rpp) replication project of this dataset, roughly one in four (22/90 = 24.4%) had a junior professor — operationalised as the senior replication-side author holding the rank “Assistant Professor” — and the figure rises to 40.0% (36/90) when the truncated rank “Assistant” is folded in (with “Researcher” never counted as junior in either case). The same accounting for the broader, discipline-based Psychology-relevant scope (Social/Cognitive studies deduplicated by study and project; 113 unique studies across ml1, ml3, and rpp) is 22/113 = 19.5% under the strict definition and 36/113 = 31.9% under the inclusive one, with all of the junior-professor share coming from the rpp cluster (ml1 and ml3 contribute 0%).
native_result.WorkflowB: The analysis uses the study-level CSV at data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (the replication-success CSV has no seniority columns and is unused). The primary scope restricts to project == 'rpp' (the only project the dataset explicitly labels 'Psychology'; all such rows have discipline in {Social, Cognitive}), defensively excludes rows with drop == True (7 of 97 dropped, denominator = 90), and counts seniority.r == 'Assistant Professor' as junior professors (Researcher never counted; the truncated rank 'Assistant' is reported only in sensitivity A). The column seniority.r is treated as the senior author of the replication study; the schema's textual description of that column is mis-labelled and was ignored in favour of the standard .o/.r (original/replication) convention. The by-project breakdown (Sensitivity B) uses a broader discipline-based Psychology scope (discipline in {Social, Cognitive}) and deduplicates ML1/ML3 multi-lab rows by (project, id); the cross-check confirmed seniority.r is constant within each (project, id) group (0 disagreements). Sensitivity C restricts the rpp denominator to replicated == 1. Outputs were persisted to analysis/summary.json and analysis/by_project_breakdown.csv.
